title: disabled vs readonly vs required
learningObjectives: Explain disabled vs readonly vs required and create accessible, secure form behaviour.

understand.concept: disabled controls are generally not focusable and are not submitted. readonly controls can remain focusable and are submitted, but users cannot edit their value. required marks a control as needing a value for constraint validation where supported.
understand.whyItMatters: These states are not interchangeable. Choosing incorrectly can cause data to be omitted or make a form difficult to use. Server-side rules must still enforce required data.
understand.analogy: Disabled is removed from the active task; readonly can be viewed but not changed; required must be completed before submission.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual validation, submission, and assistive technology behaviour follow browser and platform rules.

explain.narrative: The readonly account value is submitted, the disabled region is not, and the email field must pass required validation.

examples.code: <form><label>Account ID <input name='account' value='A-104' readonly></label><label>Region <input value='South' disabled></label><label>Email <input type='email' name='email' required></label><button>Submit</button></form>
examples.explanation: The readonly account value is submitted, the disabled region is not, and the email field must pass required validation.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered form example demonstrating the HTML behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Submit the form and inspect its data. Change each control state and record whether it can be focused, edited, and submitted.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible form with labels, constraints, clear errors, and a documented server-side validation plan. Test keyboard use and invalid values.
hints: Do not rely on colour or placeholder alone.
Client-side checks do not provide authorization or security.
Keep errors associated with their fields and easy to locate.

</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which state generally allows a value to be submitted while preventing user edits?
questions.explanation: Readonly controls are not editable by the user but are generally submitted.

questions.prompt: Which form approach is most reliable?
options: Accessible client feedback plus authoritative server validation
questions.answer: Accessible client feedback plus authoritative server validation
questions.explanation: Good forms combine user-friendly browser feedback with trusted server-side enforcement.
